description: §6.8.4 (RT) — the two-argument form `tare(@n, @factor * 2)` stores a THUNK, not a snapshot. `@factor` is bumped from 10 to 50 AFTER the tare; reset(@n) must then yield 100, not the 20 a decl-time snapshot would have frozen.
rationale: §6.8.1 is normative for the attribute form: 'The `default=` expression SHALL be evaluated AT RESET TIME, not at declaration time. The attribute stores the expression, not a snapshot.' §6.8.4 inherits that rule verbatim so the family has ONE evaluation-timing answer — two near-synonyms with divergent timing is the shape this language has rejected before. The lowering is byte-identical to the attribute's: `_scrml_default_set(key, () => <expr>)`.
